records.themeTitle: Leaving a background means discerning how to use its traits
records.themeSummary: The opening asks why the command says to go from Abraham’s land rather than simply to depart. The section will read that movement as the rectification of his own level.
records.originHebrew: "וַיֹּאמֶר ה' אֶל אַבְרָם: לֶךְ לְךָ מֵאַרְצְךָ וְגוֹמֵר אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ", יֵשׁ לְהָבִין מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "לֶךְ לְךָ מֵאַרְצְךָ", דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר "צֵא מֵאַרְצְךָ וְגוֹמֵר וְלֵךְ אֶל הָאָרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר".
records.originEnglish: “The Lord said to Abram: Go for yourself from your land … to the land that I will show you.” One must understand why it says, “Go for yourself from your land,” for it should have said, “Depart from your land … and go to the land.”
records.targetHebrew: בְּרֵאשִׁית יב, א "לֶךְ לְךָ מֵאַרְצְךָ וְגוֹמֵר", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ קֹהֶלֶת ז, א וְתַנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת וַיַּקְהֵל א: ג' שְׁלֹשָׁה שֵׁמוֹת יֵשׁ לָאָדָם: א' – שֶׁקָּרְאוּ לוֹ אֲחֵרִים, רָצָה לוֹמַר: טֶבַע הָאָדָם מַה שֶּׁלּוֹמֵד מִזּוּלָתוֹ, וְזֶהוּ "מֵאַרְצְךָ"; וְנֶגְדּוֹ: שָׁם ב "וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל" אוּמָּה שְׁלֵימָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִמִּי לִלְמוֹד, וּמִהְיוֹת הַלִּימּוּד מֵאֲחֵרִים גַּם כֵּן טוֹב שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לָלֶכֶת מִמֶּנּוּ. ב' – שֶׁקָּרָא לוֹ אָבִיו, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ה, א עֵדֻיּוֹת ב, ט: "הָאָב זוֹכֶה לַבֵּן וְכוּלֵי", וְאָמְרוּ בִּכְתוּבּוֹת סג.: "רְחֵילָא בָּתַר רְחֵילָא וְכוּלֵי", זֶהוּ "מִבֵּית אָבִיךָ"; וְנֶגְדּוֹ: "וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ" מֵאַבְרָם לְאַבְרָהָם, עַל שֵׁם: בְּרֵאשִׁית יז, ה "אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם נְתַתִּיךָ", שֶׁהוּא אָב לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ, וְגַם הַבֵּית אָב – טוֹב. ג' – שֶׁנִּקְרָא בְּסֵפֶר תּוֹלַדְתּוֹ: טֶבַע מוֹלַדְתּוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת קנו עַמּוּד א: "הַאי מַאן דִּבְמַאְדִּים וְכוּלֵי", זֶהוּ "וּמִמּוֹלַדְתְּךָ"; וְנֶגְדּוֹ: "וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ" – בְּטֶבַע תּוֹלַדְתְּךָ. וְצָרִיךְ לָלֶכֶת מֵהֶם, אֲבָל הַהֲלִיכָה – לֹא לַקָּצֶה הָאַחֲרוֹן, רַק "אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ" אֶל מָקוֹם אֲשֶׁר רוּחַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ; לִפְעָמִים רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּמִדָּה זוֹ הַנִּרְאֵית גְּרוּעָה, כַּיָּדוּעַ.
records.targetEnglish: “Go for yourself from your land,” and so forth. As written in the Midrash on Ecclesiastes and in Tanchuma, Vayakhel: A person has three names. The first is the one others call him: that is, the human disposition he learns from others. This is “from your land.” Corresponding to it is “I will make you a great nation”: an entire nation from whom to learn, so that learning from others can also be good and need not be left behind. The second is the name his father calls him, as they said, “A father confers upon his son,” and, “A ewe follows a ewe.” This is “from your father’s house.” Corresponding to it is “I will make your name great,” from Abram to Abraham, after “I have made you the father of a multitude of nations”: he is a father to the entire world, and the paternal house is also good. The third is the name recorded in the account of his birth: his inborn nature, as written in Shabbat, “One who is born under Mars,” and so forth. This is “from your birthplace.” Corresponding to it is “I will bless you”—in your inborn nature. One must go beyond these; yet the movement is not to the opposite extreme, but “to the land that I will show you,” to the place where the spirit of the blessed God directs. At times God’s will lies in that very trait which appears inferior, as is known.
records.explanation: Kometz gives a precise conceptual content to the movement questioned in the opening: acquired habits, family inheritance, and temperament require discernment. It also supplies a limit that prevents “leaving” from becoming automatic rejection of every inherited trait. This complements the next paragraph’s claim that Abraham can rectify his level from his very background; it is a conceptual comparison, not a grammatical proof of the distinction between the verbs. Citation clarification: the teaching “A father confers upon his son” is Mishnah Eduyot 2:9. The inherited Avot 5:1 locator appearing before it in the canonical Hebrew is not the source of that teaching; the Hebrew is preserved unchanged.

records.themeTitle: An idolatrous background does not own the light that emerges from it
records.themeSummary: Abraham is told that birth to Terah in an idolatrous place need not prevent his ascent. That very starting point can become the setting of his rectification.
records.originHebrew: אַךְ הָעִנְיָן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "לֶךְ לְךָ – לְאַתְקָנָא גַּרְמָךְ, לְאַתְקָנָא דַּרְגָּא דִילָךְ וְכוּלֵי", וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ, שֶׁאַף שֶׁנּוֹלַד מִתֶּרַח שֶׁהָיָה עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וּבְמָקוֹם שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁטוּפִין בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, לֹא יִפְחַד מִזֶּה, שֶׁאַדְּרַבָּה, מִזֶּה עַצְמוֹ יוּכַל לֵילֵךְ וּלְהַגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָתוֹ. וְעַד דֻּגְמַת מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם מִשָּׁם אֶת ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ וּמָצָאתָ וְגוֹמֵר", וְהוּא אַחַר שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וֶהֱפִיץ ה' אֶתְכֶם בָּעַמִּים וְגוֹמֵר", אַל יֵרַךְ לְבַבְכֶם לְהִתְיָאֵשׁ פֶּן חַס וְשָׁלוֹם תִּתְקַלְקְלוּ לְגַמְרֵי, כִּי אַדְּרַבָּה, מִשָּׁם דַּיְיקָא "וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁהַגָּלוּת יִגְרוֹם "כִּי תִדְרְשֶׁנּוּ בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכָל נַפְשֶׁךָ", וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה "וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם וּמָצָאתָ". וְכֵן אָמַר לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ: "לֶךְ לְךָ" – לְאַתְקָנָא דַּרְגָּא דִילָךְ, מֵאַרְצְךָ וּמוֹלַדְתְּךָ שֶׁנּוֹלַדְתָּ בְּמָקוֹם גָּרוּעַ וְשָׁפֵל, וּמִבֵּית אָבִיךָ שֶׁהָיָה תֶּרַח עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה – מִזֶּה עַצְמוֹ תּוּכַל לְתַקֵּן דַּרְגָּא דִילָךְ.
records.originEnglish: The matter follows what is written in the holy Zohar: “Go for yourself—to put yourself right, to put your own level right,” and so forth. God was telling him that, although he was born to Terah, an idolater, in a place immersed in idolatry, he should not fear this. On the contrary, from that very situation he could advance and reach his level. This resembles “From there you shall seek the Lord your God, and you shall find Him,” which follows “The Lord will scatter you among the peoples.” Do not lose heart and despair, fearing that, God forbid, you will become completely corrupted. On the contrary, precisely “from there you shall seek”: the exile will bring about “when you seek Him with all your heart and all your soul,” and thereby “you shall seek and find.” So too, the blessed God told our father Abraham: “Go for yourself”—to put your own level right—“from your land and your birthplace,” having been born in a degraded, lowly place, “and from your father’s house,” Terah having been an idolater. From that very situation you can put your level right.
records.targetRef: Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 15:2

records.targetEnglish: However, this follows what is explained in the holy Zohar: “Their light is withheld from the wicked”—this is Terah and his household; “their light”—this is Abraham. It does not say “the light,” but “their light,” for it had been with them. The Zohar explains that, since the blessed God arranged for all influence to proceed through cause and effect, with the later stage drawn from the earlier one—as it says, “Generation to generation shall praise Your works,” each generation being the head of the next—there would seem to be a connection between Abraham’s light and Terah his father, since Terah was a cause of Abraham. Therefore the Zohar says, “Their light is withheld from the wicked”—Terah and his household; “their light”—Abraham. A person’s acquisition in anything extends only as far as his grasp of it; beyond his grasp he has no acquisition in it. Thus Hagahot Asheri rules in the name of Rabbi Eliezer of Metz: one who bought silver coated with lead, not knowing it was silver and buying it on the assumption that it was tin or lead, acquired only the value of tin or lead. So Terah has no share in Abraham’s light, for he had no grasp of it, being an idolater. The ten generations from Noah to Abraham are therefore not called our fathers: they had no grasp of Abraham’s preciousness and no connection or attachment to him. Abraham’s birth from Terah follows only the Sages’ statement, “Through everything the Holy One carries out His mission”; he is not on that account to be attributed to Terah.
records.explanation: Sod Yesharim distinguishes being a historical cause from possessing a share in the spiritual light that comes through that cause. This explains why Terah’s idolatry does not set the limit of Abraham’s possible identity. Peri Tzadik emphasizes the movement of rectification from a low starting point; Sod explains why that starting point cannot claim ownership of the resulting light.

records.themeTitle: Prayer is needed where even spiritual understanding can fail
records.themeSummary: The second altar addresses guidance that remains concealed from a person. Abraham and Isaac themselves could intend an outcome that God had to redirect; in that sphere, Rav Tzadok names prayer as the necessary response.
records.originHebrew: אַךְ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ אִיתָא (פ עַמּוּד א): "וּבָנָה תְּרֵין מַדְבְּחָן, חַד לְדַרְגָּא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא וְחַד לְדַרְגָּא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא וְכוּלֵי, וּכְדֵין אִתְעַטַּר אַבְרָהָם מִדַּרְגָּא לְדַרְגָּא עַד דִּסְלִיק לְדַרְגֵּיהּ וְכוּלֵי", וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁתֵּי מַדְרֵגוֹת: "דַּרְגָּא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא" הוּא מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם בּוֹ תְּפִיסָה וְהַבָנָה, וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה; וְ"דַרְגָּא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא" – מַה שֶּׁנֶּעְלָם הַהַנְהָגָה מִן הָאָדָם, עַד דֻּגְמַת מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי ה' יִהְיֶה בְכִסְלֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר", וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י מִיְרוּשַׁלְמִי: "בִּדְבָרִים שֶׁאַתָּה כְּסִיל בָּהֶם". וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל יִשְׁמָעֵאל: "לוּ יִשְׁמָעֵאל יִחְיֶה לְפָנֶיךָ", וְכֵן יִצְחָק שֶׁרָצָה לְבָרֵךְ אֶת עֵשָׂו, וְהוֹרָה לָהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתָּם, וְעַל זֶה אֵין שׁוּם עֵצָה רַק תְּפִלָּה לַה', וְאָז "וְשָׁמַר רַגְלְךָ מִלָּכֶד". וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ: "וַיִּבֶן שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ לַה'" וְלֹא כְּתִיב "הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלָיו", וְהַיְינוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא; וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיִּקְרָא בְּשֵׁם ה'", וְתַרְגּוּם אוּנְקְלוֹס: "וְצַלִּי בִּשְׁמָא דַּה'", שֶׁעַל זֶה נִצְרָךְ תְּפִלָּה.
records.originEnglish: The holy Zohar states: “He built two altars, one for the revealed level and one for the concealed level … and then Abraham was crowned from level to level until he rose to his own level.” There are two levels. The revealed level is what a person can grasp and understand, and this comes through words of Torah. The concealed level is where the direction of events is hidden from a person, like “The Lord will be your confidence, and will guard your foot from being caught.” Rashi explains from the Jerusalem Talmud: “In matters in which you lack understanding.” This was so with our father Abraham, who prayed concerning Ishmael, “If only Ishmael might live before You,” and likewise Isaac, who wished to bless Esau. The blessed God guided them apart from their own understanding. For this there is no counsel except prayer to God; then “He will guard your foot from being caught.” Thus it later says, “He built an altar there to the Lord,” without saying, “Who appeared to him”: this is the concealed level. And so it says, “He called upon the name of the Lord,” which Onkelos translates, “He prayed in the name of the Lord,” for this requires prayer.

records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach explains why a high spiritual level does not eliminate the need for the second altar. records.originEnglish: It then says, “Journeying onward toward the south.” Abraham our father’s level was love, and his attribute was kindness. His entire work was to refine his love so that it would be pure, for the blessed God alone, and no desire for this world’s affairs would enter his heart. This is “journeying toward the south,” following the exposition, “For you have given me a dry land”—a house dried of all good. Abraham’s level was the refinement of his attribute of kindness, so that it would be pure for God and no desire for this world’s affairs would be mixed into it. This also explains what is said of Isaac, whose attribute was the fear of Isaac and restraint: “He was dwelling in the land of the south.” He was at ease in this attribute, being refined in restraint, fear, and awe.

records.targetEnglish: “God made this corresponding to that”: the blessed God gave a person the choice either to benefit another through kindness and to execute judgment against the wicked, or to benefit himself through evil desires—as the Baal Shem Tov explained, “A person’s desire is his kindness”—and to benefit God’s enemies, as is known, that an adulterer can be good to other people. “Do not murder” and “Do not commit adultery” are two opposites, as I have written elsewhere. records.explanation: Kometz shows why even kindness needs refinement: the same expansive power can serve another person or feed one’s own appetite, just as strength can become either just restraint or destructive aggression. This gives a mechanism for Rav Tzadok’s repeated concern that Abraham’s love remain unmixed, without treating kindness itself as the defect.

His enemies became his footstool: he brought light out of darkness, even from the left side. records.explanation: Beit Yaakov reads the same southward movement as restraint that serves the search for divine light. records.themeTitle: An apparently unsuccessful prayer may still bear fruit
records.themeSummary: Rav Tzadok asks why Abraham’s prayer at Ai is emphasized when it did not completely prevent the later loss. The question concerns the effect and enduring significance of that prayer.
records.originHebrew: וּבִמְדְרַשׁ רַבָּה הוּבָא בְּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל בָּעַי עַל זַרְעוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִפְּלוּ בָּעַי, וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין לָמָּה נִזְכַּר כָּאן תְּפִלָּתוֹ, כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא הוֹעִילָה לְגַמְרֵי, שֶׁהֲרֵי נָפְלוּ שָׁם שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשִׁשָּׁה אִישׁ? גַּם אִם הָיָה הַמְּכֻוָּון "וַיִּקְרָא בְּשֵׁם ה'" עַל תְּפִלָּה זוֹ, לֹא יוּבַן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּשׁוּבוֹ מִמִּצְרַיִם: "אֶל מְקוֹם הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּקְרָא שָׁם אַבְרָם בְּשֵׁם ה'", וְלָמָּה צִיֵּיר הַמִּזְבֵּחַ בְּסִימָן זֶה שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל שָׁם?
records.originEnglish: Midrash Rabbah, cited in Rashi’s commentary, says that he prayed at Ai for his descendants, that they should not fall at Ai. One must understand why his prayer is mentioned here when it did not help completely, for thirty-six men fell there. Moreover, if “He called upon the name of the Lord” referred to this prayer, what is the meaning of the account of his return from Egypt: “To the place of the altar … and there Abram called upon the name of the Lord”? Why identify the altar by this sign, that he had prayed there?
records.targetHebrew: כִּי הַאֻמְנָם אָמְרוּ לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא הוֹעִילָה תְּפִלָּתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם, בְּכָל זֹאת הָיָה לִבּוֹ נָכוֹן וּבָטוּחַ כִּי תְּפִלַּת אַבְרָהָם לֹא תָּשׁוּב רֵיקָם וְהָעֵת עֵת רָצוֹן, וּמַה שֶּׁיְּבַקֵּשׁ עַתָּה יִנָּתֵן לוֹ.
records.targetEnglish: For although [the angels] told [Lot] that Abraham’s prayer had not availed, his heart nevertheless remained firm and confident that Abraham’s prayer would not return empty, that this was a time of favor, and that whatever he now asked would be given to him.
records.explanation: In Beit Yaakov’s full account, the failure to save Sodom does not make Abraham’s prayer fruitless: hearing of it moves Lot to petition for Zoar. This exposes the assumption behind Rav Tzadok’s question about Ai. A prayer’s effect need not coincide completely with its apparent first aim. Rav Tzadok’s own continuation gives a different concrete effect—its benefit to Abraham himself—so the two outcomes must not be conflated.

records.themeTitle: Torah can become the person’s own inward speech
records.themeSummary: The first altar preserves a place for attaining Oral Torah. Abraham’s Torah arose from within: his own kidneys are described as teachers of Torah and wisdom.
records.originHebrew: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיִּבֶן שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ לַה' הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלָיו", וְהוּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוּשְׁאַר שָׁם מָקוֹם קָבוּעַ וְקָדוֹשׁ לְהַשִּׂיג שָׁם תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה עִיקַּר תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, שֶׁהִשִּׂיג הַכֹּל מִלִּבּוֹ, שֶׁכִּלְיוֹתָיו נַעֲשׂוּ כִּשְׁנֵי רַבָּנִים וּמְלַמְּדוֹת אוֹתוֹ תּוֹרָה וְחָכְמָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סא).
records.originEnglish: This is “He built an altar there to the Lord Who appeared to him.” It was so that a fixed, holy place should remain there for attaining Oral Torah. This was the essential character of Abraham our father’s Torah: he attained everything from his heart, his kidneys becoming like two teachers who taught him Torah and wisdom, as written in Bereshit Rabbah.
records.targetHebrew: וּמִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב שָׁם: אַגְמִירוּ וְכוּלֵי כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלִיגְרְסוּ, נִרְאֶה דִּבְהַתְחָלָה צָרִיךְ לְיַגֵּעַ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ דְּבָרִים הַיּוֹצְאִים מִן הַלֵּב; אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ זוֹכֶה לְדִבּוּר וְגִירְסָא הֲגַם דְּלָא יָדַע מַאי קָאָמַר, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא פִּטְטַיָּא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, גַּם כֵּן הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה גָּמוּר. וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (שָׁם): בַּתְּחִלָּה תּוֹרַת ה', וְאַחַר כָּךְ תּוֹרָתוֹ; וּכְשֶׁזּוֹכֶה דְּהוּא תּוֹרָתוֹ, דּוּגְמַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נַעֲשׂוּ שְׁתֵּי כִּלְיוֹתָיו וְכוּלֵי (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סא), גַּם דִּבּוּר שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה. וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּדוֹאֵג בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קו:) שֶׁכָּל תּוֹרָתוֹ וְכוּלֵי מִשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ, הַיְינוּ בְּלֹא הָיָה לוֹ הַהַתְחָלָה; וְגַם כִּי עַל יְדֵי לָשׁוֹן הָרָע נִתְקַלְקֵל הַדִּבּוּר שֶׁמֵּהַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ.
records.targetEnglish: From the statement there, “Teach them … so that they may recite,” it appears that at the beginning one must labor so that the words come from the heart. Afterward one merits speech and recitation even when one does not know what one is saying; what is called the chatter of Torah is then also fully words of Torah. This is “At first it is the Torah of the Lord, and afterward his own Torah.” When he merits that it is his Torah—like Abraham our father, whose two kidneys became [teachers]—even speech that is only from the lips outward is words of Torah. What is said of Doeg, that all his Torah was only from the lips outward, concerns someone who lacked that beginning. Moreover, slander corrupted the speech that was from the lips outward.
records.explanation: Tzidkat explains the development behind the image of Abraham’s inward teachers. Torah becomes “his own” after an initial labor that brings its words into the heart; only on that basis can even apparently spontaneous recitation express Torah. The contrast with Doeg preserves the qualification: outward fluency by itself is not the inward Torah described in Peri Tzadik.

records.themeTitle: A sacred encounter leaves a place of return
records.themeSummary: The first altar retains the holiness of the revelation. Rav Tzadok explains that an encounter with the Divine Presence leaves an enduring impression that can still be accessed after its original moment.
records.originHebrew: וְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ הַשְׁרָאַת הַשְּׁכִינָה נִשְׁאָר הַקְּדוּשָׁה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד, שֶׁהָרְשִׁימוּ נִשְׁאָר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (יוֹמָא לט עַמּוּד ב): "פַּעַם אַחַת הָלַכְתִּי לְשִׁילֹה וְהֵרַחְתִּי רֵיחַ קְטוֹרֶת מִבֵּין כְּתָלֶיהָ", שֶׁאַף שֶׁכְּבָר חָרְבָה שִׁילֹה יָמִים רַבִּים נִשְׁאַר הָרְשִׁימוּ דִּקְדוּשָׁה וְהֵרִיחוּ רֵיחַ קְטוֹרֶת. וְזֶה עִנְיַן מִזְבֵּחַ רִאשׁוֹן – מְקוֹם תּוֹרָה.
records.originEnglish: Wherever the Divine Presence rests, holiness remains forever, for the impression remains. Thus we find: “Once I went to Shiloh and smelled the scent of incense between its walls.” Although Shiloh had already lain destroyed for many years, the impression of holiness remained and they smelled the scent of incense. This is the meaning of the first altar: a place of Torah.
records.targetHebrew: ואח"כ התפלל אאע"ה אשר יאמר היום בהר ד' יראה, והיינו שאם אדם ירצה לעבוד את השי"ת יהיה ביכולת בניקל לעורר את זאת הקדושה הנשאר מעבודת העקידה.
records.targetEnglish: Afterward Abraham our father prayed: “As it is said today, On the mountain of the Lord He shall be seen.” This means that if a person wishes to serve the blessed God, it should be possible for him easily to awaken that holiness which remains from the service of the Binding.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef states the practical consequence of a lasting holy impression: Abraham’s later prayer makes the holiness of the Binding available to someone who wishes to serve God. This clarifies why Peri Tzadik treats the first altar as an enduring place of attainment, rather than only as a monument to a revelation that has passed.

records.themeTitle: Receiving wealth requires a fresh examination of motive
records.themeSummary: After accepting gifts in Egypt, Abraham returns to prayer because his new possessions could awaken worldly desire. Earlier refinement does not remove the need to examine a changed situation.
records.originHebrew: וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס לְמִצְרַיִם, עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ, וְיָצָא מִשָּׁם עִם הַמַּתָּנוֹת, כְּתִיב: "וַיַּעַל אַבְרָם מִמִּצְרַיִם וְגוֹמֵר הַנֶּגְבָּה", וּכְתִיב: "וְאַבְרָם כָּבֵד מְאֹד בַּמִּקְנֶה וְגוֹמֵר", וּפֵירֵשׁ רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זְצוּקַלְלָהּ"ה שֶׁהָיָה כָּבֵד עָלָיו וּלְמַשָּׂא כְּבֵדָה הַקִּנְיָנִים שֶׁקָּנָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּתְיָירֵא פֶּן יִכָּנֵס בְּלִבּוֹ חֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ, דְּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי כְּתִיב "הַנֶּגְבָּה" שָׁם. וּכְתִיב: "וַיֵּלֶךְ וְגוֹמֵר אֶל מְקוֹם הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּקְרָא שָׁם אַבְרָם בְּשֵׁם ה'", וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהָלַךְ לְשָׁם לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עוֹד שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנֵס הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְהַסְטִינוֹ.
records.originEnglish: Afterward, when he entered Egypt, “the nakedness of the land,” and left with the gifts, it is written, “Abram went up from Egypt ... toward the south,” and, “Abram was very heavy in livestock,” and so forth. Our holy master, of blessed memory, explained that the possessions he had acquired weighed upon him as a heavy burden, because he feared that desire for this world might enter his heart. This follows what we have explained, and is why “toward the south” is written there. It is also written, “He went ... to the place of the altar ... and there Abram called upon the name of the Lord.” This means that he went there to pray again that the evil inclination should not enter and lead him astray.
records.targetRef: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 10:8
records.targetHebrew: וְגַם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ גָּלָה לְמִצְרַיִם, וְהוּא אֶחָד מִנִּסְיוֹנוֹתָיו; שֶׁהָיוּ הַנִּסְיוֹנוֹת בֵּירוּר מִדַּת הָאֵיתָנוּת שֶׁלּוֹ שֶׁהוּא לִרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהָרְאָיָה – שֶׁלִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵינוֹ עַקְשָׁן, וּמַעֲבִיר עַל דַּעְתּוֹ וְגוֹלֶה לְמִצְרַיִם, שֶׁזֶּהוּ כֹּחַ לֵב בָּשָׂר וְהֵיפֶךְ עַקְשָׁנוּת. וּלְכָךְ שָׁם קִבֵּל מַתָּנוֹת, וּמֵרְכוּשׁ סְדוֹם לֹא רָצָה לֵיהָנוֹת; כִּי שָׁם הָיָה מִצַּד מִדַּת לֵב בָּשָׂר, וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּעִקְּשׁוּת הוּא גַּם כֵּן מוּתָּר לֵיהָנוֹת מִזֶּה; מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מַעֲשֵׂה דִּמְלָכִים הָיָה עִקְּשׁוּת גָּדוֹל לְמַרְאִית עַיִן, לִהְיוֹת יָחִיד נִלְחָם נֶגֶד ד' מְלָכִים בִּשְׁבִיל לוֹט בֶּן אָחִיו, מַה שֶּׁלֹּא עָשָׂה כֵּן בְּמִצְרַיִם לִהְיוֹת נִלְחָם נֶגְדָּם בִּשְׁבִיל אִשְׁתּוֹ הָאֲהוּבָה לוֹ יוֹתֵר; וּלְכָךְ בָּזֶה לֹא רָצָה לֵיהָנוֹת, כִּי בְּדָבָר שֶׁהוּא עִקְּשׁוּת צָרִיךְ בֵּירוּר אִם אֵינוֹ עִקְּשׁוּת לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ, רַק לִכְבוֹד שָׁמַיִם.
records.targetEnglish: Abraham our father also went into exile in Egypt, and this was one of his trials. The trials clarified that his firmness served the blessed God’s will. The proof was that, in response to God’s will, he was not obstinate: he set aside his own opinion and went into exile in Egypt. This is the power of a heart of flesh, the opposite of obstinacy. Therefore he received gifts there, whereas he did not wish to benefit from Sodom’s property. There [in Egypt] the matter came from the attribute of a heart of flesh, without obstinacy, so it was also permitted to enjoy its benefit. The episode of the kings, however, appeared outwardly to involve great obstinacy: one man fought four kings for his nephew Lot, something he had not done in Egypt for his wife, whom he loved more. Therefore in this case he did not wish to benefit, for in a matter that involves obstinacy one must clarify whether it is obstinacy for one’s own enjoyment or only for the honor of Heaven.
records.explanation: Likkutei distinguishes the acceptance of Egyptian gifts from the refusal of Sodom’s wealth by examining the motive within each episode. This keeps Peri Tzadik’s description of wealth as a burden precise: possessions require renewed discernment, but receiving a benefit is not automatically the same as craving it. The new prayer addresses the risk that a previously obedient act will later feed self-interest.

records.themeTitle: Torah and prayer are two forms of Jacob’s voice
records.themeSummary: The two altars become a pattern for the voices of Torah and prayer in Israel. Together they are means of repairing the corruption symbolized by the serpent.
records.originHebrew: וּשְׁנֵי הַמִּזְבְּחוֹת הֵם כְּנֶגֶד קוֹלוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב בְּבָתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת וּבְבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת, דִּכְתִיב: "הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב": "קָל" חָסֵר וָא"ו שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל תְּפִלָּה, "קוֹל" מָלֵא וָא"ו – קוֹל תּוֹרָה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל לְתַקֵּן כָּל קִלְקוּל הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהוּא לוֹט.
records.originEnglish: The two altars correspond to Jacob’s voice in synagogues and study houses, as it says, “The voice is the voice of Jacob.” The first kol, written without a vav, points to prayer; the second kol, written with a vav, is the voice of Torah. Through this one can repair all the corruption of the serpent, represented by Lot.
records.targetHebrew: כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּאֵין כֹּחָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא בְּפִיהֶם (בַּמִּדְבָּר פָּרָשָׁה כ׳, וּמִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים כ״ב, וּמְכִילְתָּא בְּשַׁלַּח פָּרָשָׁה ב׳, וְזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וַיִּשְׁלַח קע״ח עַמּוּד א׳, וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת), שֶׁהוּא "הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב" [בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ״ב], שְׁנֵי קוֹלוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (דִּפְתִיחְתָּא דְּאֵיכָה רַבָּתִי): בְּבָתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת וּבְבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת, הַיְינוּ קוֹל תְּפִלָּה הָרָמוּז בְּמִלַּת "הַקֹּל" חֲסַר וָא״ו בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב, וּבְתוֹסֶפֶת הַהֵ״א הָרוֹמֶזֶת לִתְפִלָּה כַּנּוֹדָע, וְ"קוֹל" מָלֵא וָא״ו רוֹמֵז לְקוֹל תּוֹרָה כַּיָּדוּעַ, דְּהַוָּא״ו רוֹמֶזֶת עַל זֶה (עַיֵּן בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וַיִּגַּשׁ ר״י רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳, וְרֵישׁ וַיִּקְרָא), וְהַשּׁוֹפָר הוּא רוֹמֵז הִתְעוֹרְרוּת קוֹל שׁוֹפָר דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא הַקּוֹל תּוֹרָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ עֲלֵיהֶם לְטוֹבָה.
records.targetEnglish: As is known, Israel’s power is only in their mouth: “The voice is the voice of Jacob.” These are the two voices which the Sages locate in synagogues and study houses: the voice of prayer, alluded to by the first kol, written without a vav, together with its added he, which alludes to prayer; and the second kol, written with a vav, which alludes to the voice of Torah, as is known. The shofar alludes to the awakening of the shofar’s voice at the giving of Torah, the voice of Torah present in Jacob’s descendants. Through this His providence extends over them for good.
records.explanation: Poked Akarim applies the same two voices to the community’s Rosh Hashanah service: the shofar awakens the inherited voice of Torah and draws providence for good. It develops the step Peri Tzadik makes from Abraham’s two altars to a pattern available to every Israelite, without treating the two altar episodes as only private biography.

records.themeTitle: Seven attributes are the channels through which blessing is received
records.themeSummary: Rav Tzadok relates the seven blessings to the seven attributes of creation and to the shepherds who embody them. The number describes the ordered reception of divine influence.
records.originHebrew: בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (סִטְרֵי תּוֹרָה עח עַמּוּד א) חָשַׁב שֶׁבַע בְּרָכוֹת: "'וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל' – הַאי בִּרְכָתָא חֲדָא וְכוּלֵי, 'וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ וְגוֹמֵר' – הָא שֶׁבַע". וּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִסְפַּר שֶׁבַע הֵם כְּנֶגֶד שֶׁבַע הַמִּדּוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "שִׁבְעָה מִי יוֹדֵעַ וְכוּלֵי שִׁבְעָה יְמֵי שַׁבַּתָּא", וְהַמְּכֻוָּון שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּזְכַּר מִסְפַּר שֶׁבַע הֵם כְּנֶגֶד שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית שֶׁהֵם שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת תַּחְתּוֹנִיּוֹת; וּכְנֶגֶד שֶׁבַע הַמִּדּוֹת – שִׁבְעָה רוֹעִים שֶׁהֵם מֶרְכָּבָה לְהַמִּדּוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּזֹהַר חָדָשׁ תּוֹלְדוֹת), וְכֵן הוּא סֵדֶר הַבְּרָכוֹת כָּאן.
records.originEnglish: The holy Zohar, Sitrei Torah, counts seven blessings: “I will make you a great nation”—this is one blessing … “All [families] shall be blessed through you”—these are seven. Wherever there is the number seven, it corresponds to the seven attributes, as we say, “Who knows seven? … The seven days of the week.” The meaning is that wherever the number seven is mentioned, it corresponds to the seven days of creation, which are the seven lower attributes. Corresponding to the seven attributes are the seven shepherds, who are a chariot for those attributes, as stated in Zohar Chadash, Toldot. This is also the order of the blessings here.
records.targetHebrew: הענין בזה, דהנה כל הטובות שבעולם הזה מלובשים דרך שבע מדות שהציב השי"ת בזה העולם, כמו שכתיב (דברי הימים א כ״ט:י״א) לך ד' הגדולה והגבורה וגו' עד לך ד' הממלכה, שמורה על מדת מלכות שמים. ובאם האדם השיג כבר הטובה הנכלל מתוך כל שבע המדות, ועוד מכיר שהטובה עדיין הוא בידו ית', לא שהשי"ת מסר כבר הטובה מרשותו, אלא שהוא עדיין גם כעת בידו ית' והוא רק זוכה משלחן גבוה, אז יש להאדם קנין גמור בהטובה, ואז יש לו קנין של אמת בהטובה שהשיג מאת השי"ת. וכמו שאיתא בש"ס (ברכות לה.) רבי לוי רמי כתיב לד' הארץ ומלואה וכתיב והארץ נתן לבני אדם, לא קשיא כאן קודם ברכה כאן לאחר ברכה, והיינו לאחר ברכה מורה, שמכיר שד' הוא הנותן של הטובה והטובה הוא בידו ית', שזה מורה ברכה, אז יש לאדם קנין גמור בהטובה ונקרא והארץ נתן לבני אדם.
records.targetEnglish: The matter is this: all the good things in this world are clothed through the seven attributes that the blessed God established in this world, as it says, “Yours, Lord, are greatness and strength … Yours, Lord, is the kingdom,” indicating the attribute of the kingdom of Heaven. If a person has already attained the good included within all seven attributes, and still recognizes that the good remains in God’s hand—that God has not already transferred it out of His domain, but that even now it remains in His hand and the person receives only from the table on high—then the person has a complete acquisition of that good. He then has a true acquisition of the good he received from God. Thus the Talmud states: Rabbi Levi raised a contradiction: it is written, “The earth and its fullness belong to the Lord,” and it is written, “He has given the earth to human beings.” There is no difficulty: one is before a blessing, the other after a blessing. “After a blessing” indicates recognition that God is the giver of the good and that the good remains in His hand. This is what a blessing indicates. Then a person has a complete acquisition of the good, and it is called, “He has given the earth to human beings.”
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains what the sevenfold order accomplishes: the attributes are channels through which good becomes available within the world. Recognizing its continuing divine source makes receiving that good truthful. This gives substance to Rav Tzadok’s mapping of seven blessings to seven attributes; it does not identify each blessing with a new shepherd or claim that the Emor passage makes that mapping.

records.themeTitle: Abraham reaches his root through successive refinement
records.themeSummary: The blessing of greatness without measure corresponds to Abraham’s love becoming clarified up to its supernal root. “Advanced in days” names that attainment.
records.originHebrew: "וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל" – הַיְינוּ בְּלֹא שִׁיעוּר, שֶׁכֵּן מוֹרֶה לְשׁוֹן "גָּדוֹל", וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ שֶׁזָּכָה בְּמִדָּתוֹ עַד כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן, כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "בְּאִינּוּן יוֹמִין עִלָּאִין וְכוּלֵי", וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר בְּמִדָּתוֹ שֶׁהִיא הָאַהֲבָה עַד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ בְּג' רִאשׁוֹנוֹת.
records.originEnglish: “I will make you a great nation” means without measure, for this is what the expression “great” indicates. It corresponds to Abraham our father, who merited through his attribute to reach the supernal crown, as it says, “Abraham was old, advanced in days,” and as the holy Zohar writes, “In those supernal days ….” That is, he became clarified in his attribute, which is love, up to its root in the first three [sefirot].
records.targetRef: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Chayei Sara 24:1
records.targetHebrew: וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים וְהַשֵּׁם בֵּרַךְ אֶת אַבְרָהָם בַּכֹּל. זָקֵן מוֹרֶה שֶׁזֶּה קָנָה חָכְמָה, וְיֵשׁ לוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה בִּקְבִיעוּת וְאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְצִמְצוּמִים עוֹד. וְזֶה בָּא לוֹ אַחַר עֲקֵידַת יִצְחָק, וְאַחַר שֶׁנִּמּוֹל, וְנִתְנַסָּה עֶשֶׂר נִסְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁלֹּא נִתְנַסָּה שׁוּם בְּרִיָּה בָּעוֹלָם, וְנִשְׁתַּנָּה מֵהֵיפֶךְ לְהֵיפֶךְ, כְּעִנְיַן גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהִתְהַפֵּךְ וּלְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת מֵהֵיפֶךְ לְהֵיפֶךְ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּרְגַּל עַל דֶּרֶךְ לֹא טוֹב עַד עַתָּה. וְכֵן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בָּא אֶל הַשְּׁלֵימוּת וְנִשְׁתַּנָּה מִכְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה עַד עַתָּה שֶׁהָיָה צָרִיךְ לַעֲבוֹדוֹת וְצִמְצוּמִים, וְעַתָּה נִקְבְּעָה בּוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה בִּקְבִיעוּת שֶׁלֹּא יִצְרַךְ עוֹד לַעֲבוֹדוֹת וְצִמְצוּמִים. וּלְזוֹ הַמַּדְרֵגָה לֹא יוּכַל אָדָם לָבֹא רַק בְּהַדְרָגָה, וְעַל זֶה מוֹרֶה בָּא בַּיָּמִים, כְּפִי תְּפִיסַת הָאָדָם, כִּדְאִיתָא בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חַיֵּי קכט.) וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים וְכוּלֵי בְּאִינוּן יוֹמִין עִלָּאִין בְּאִינוּן יוֹמִין יְדִיעָאן וְכוּלֵי. וְזֶה הוּא דְּאִיתָא בְּשִׁשָּׁה סְדָרִים (עֵירוּבִין נו.) כָּל עִיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ מַעֲלוֹת וּמוֹרָדוֹת מַזְקִינִים בַּחֲצִי יְמֵיהֶם, שֶׁבְּטֶבַע זֶה הָעוֹלָם הוּא, שֶׁאִם יְהַלֵּךְ אָדָם בְּדֶרֶךְ יָשָׁר לְאַט לְאַט אָזַי לֹא יַזְקִין בַּחֲצִי יָמָיו. וְכֵן הוּא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה גַּם כֵּן, שֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעַ אָדָם אֶל הַשְּׁלֵימוּת אַךְ בְּהַדְרָגָה, שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים נִרְאֶה לוֹ לָאָדָם שֶׁהוּא בְּמַדְרֵגָה גְּדוֹלָה, וְאַחַר זֶה רוֹאֶה חֶסְרוֹן בְּעַצְמוֹ וּמִתְחַזֵּק עַל יְדֵי זֶה בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְתַקֵּן אֶת זֶה הַחֶסְרוֹן, וְהוּא כְּעִנְיַן גְּעָרָה, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַגְּעָרָה מִתְחַזֵּק הָאָדָם בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כָּל פַּעַם עוֹד יוֹתֵר, עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ אֶל עִיקַּר שְׁלֵימוּתוֹ.
records.targetEnglish: “Abraham was old, advanced in days, and the Lord had blessed Abraham in everything.” “Old” indicates one who has acquired wisdom: holiness is established in him, and he no longer needs restraints. This came to him after the Binding of Isaac, after he was circumcised and underwent ten trials such as no other creature in the world underwent. He changed from one opposite to the other, like a convert who must turn and change from one opposite to the other, having until then been accustomed to a way that was not good. So Abraham our father attained completeness and changed from his previous condition, when he had needed acts of service and restraint. Now holiness became established in him, so that he would no longer need those acts and restraints. A person can reach this level only gradually. This is what “advanced in days” indicates, within human apprehension, as the holy Zohar states: “Abraham was old, advanced in days … in those supernal days, in those known days ….” This is the teaching in the Six Orders: “Any town that has ascents and descents causes people to age at half their days.” The nature of this world is that, if a person walks on a level path slowly, he does not age at half his days. So too in words of Torah: a person reaches completeness only gradually. Sometimes he seems to himself to be on a great level; afterward he sees a lack in himself and thereby strengthens himself in serving God to repair that lack. This is like a rebuke, through which a person becomes stronger in words of Torah each time, until he reaches his essential completeness.
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov reads the same “supernal days” through Abraham’s successive trials and repeated discovery of what still needs repair. It explains how the attainment described briefly by Rav Tzadok can become established in the person. The cessation of restraint belongs to the completed level in the quoted account; it is not presented as advice to skip the gradual work.

records.themeTitle: Oral Torah supplies the greater wisdom needed after damage
records.themeSummary: Isaac’s blessing is explained through restraint and the removal of evil. Oral Torah is the expanding wisdom that repairs the anger and damage which have entered the world.
records.originHebrew: "וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ" – תְּרֵין, נֶגֶד יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ פַּחַד יִצְחָק, וְהַיְינוּ לְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּמִצְווֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ", וְהוּא לְהוֹרִיק הָרַע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל, לִהְיוֹת אִתְפַּנֵּי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִתַּמָּן. וְזֶה עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא "הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה" לְתַקֵּן "הַרְבֵּה כָּעַס". וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִקְרֵאת "בְּרָכָה", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ סֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר שֶׁכָּתַב: "וּמְנָלָן שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה אִקְּרֵי בְּרָכָה וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'יָם וְדָרוֹם יְרָשָׁה', וּכְתִיב: 'רְחָבָה מִנִּי יָם'", עַיֵּין שָׁם, וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, דְּהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב מְנוּיָה וּסְפוּרָה אוֹתִיּוֹתֶיהָ.
records.originEnglish: “I will bless you”—the second [blessing]—corresponds to Isaac our father, whose attribute is the fear of Isaac. It means becoming clarified in the prohibitions, whose root is “You shall have no other [gods]”: emptying evil from the fool’s heart, so that the evil inclination is removed from there. This occurs through Oral Torah, which is “much wisdom” to repair “much anger.” Oral Torah is called “blessing,” as written at the beginning of Sefer HaBahir: “From where do we know that Torah is called blessing? … As it says, ‘Possess the sea and the south,’ and it is written, ‘Broader than the sea.’” See there. This means Oral Torah, for the letters of Written Torah are numbered and counted.
records.targetHebrew: וְזֶהוּ הַשַּׁעַר הָרָאוּי כְּפִי מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה לִהְיוֹת "בָּרוּךְ מִכָּל הָעַמִּים" [דְּבָרִים ז׳:י״ד], שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, שֶׁהוּא הַדְּפוּס שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהָיָה תְּחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה. וְאַלְמָלֵא זָכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, לֹא נִתְּנָה לָהֶם אֶלָּא הַתּוֹרָה וְסֵפֶר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּלְבַד, כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּנְדָרִים (כ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳). וְכָל שְׁאָר הַנַּ״ךְ וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא מִצַּד הַקִּלְקוּלִים, וּמֵרֹב כַּעַס הֻצְרְכוּ לְרֹב חָכְמָה.
records.targetEnglish: This is the gate appropriate according to the judgment of Torah: to be “blessed above all the peoples.” This is the judgment of Written Torah, which is the pattern of the work of creation as it was at the beginning of creation. Had Israel merited, only the Torah and the Book of Joshua would have been given to them, as stated in Nedarim. All the remaining Prophets and Writings, and all the more so Oral Torah, come on account of the corruptions: because of much anger, much wisdom was required.
records.explanation: Poked distinguishes the original pattern of creation from the additional wisdom required once damage has occurred. This makes Rav Tzadok’s phrase “much wisdom to repair much anger” an account of why Oral Torah expands, rather than a claim that anger itself is the desired state. Poked’s surrounding discussion concerns different forms of deliverance and judgment; that framework is not imported into Isaac’s blessing.

records.targetEnglish: “‘I will bless you’—this is our saying, ‘God of Isaac’”: from the side of strength, Isaac’s level. He clarified matters in the world and broke through all concealments, returning all matters to the blessed God, joining them to their root, and recognizing that everything is His. From his attribute branches out all a person’s wealth and property: through his service and restraints it is called by his name, for through the labor of his hands he has merited God’s abundance. Since he serves God, overcomes his heart’s desire, and breaks through all concealments to join and attach all matters to their root, God says that the line of justice indeed requires the power of the root to be in the branches—in the creatures who serve Him. It is to be called by their name, as though they themselves accomplished all this through their handiwork. This is what “I will bless you” indicates, from the Talmudic expression for layering a plant: what was layered grew.
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov explains why Isaac’s restraint is productive: it breaks the concealment that makes possessions appear detached from God and reconnects the branches to their root. Its interpretation of blessing through the growth of a layered plant gives a concrete image for gain through restraint. Peri Tzadik supplies the more specific instrument, Oral Torah; Beit Yaakov does not name that instrument in this paragraph.

records.themeTitle: Jacob’s completeness clarifies the holiness inherited from the fathers
records.themeSummary: Jacob’s wholly included line makes the promise to Abraham enduring and clarifies which descendants express the ancestral holiness. Rav Tzadok therefore says that the earlier fathers too are called Israel.
records.originHebrew: "וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ" – נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, שֶׁהוּא פָּעַל שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ", שֶׁאָז נִתְפַּשֵּׁט קְדֻשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מִדַּת גְּדוּלָּה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד, "שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד", שֶׁאָז כְּבָר יָצָא הַפְּסֹלֶת, וְאָז נִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁגַּם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, שֶׁעֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל לֹא נֶחְשַׁב זַרְעוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיִצְחָק "וְלֹא כָּל יִצְחָק", וְאַחַר לֵידַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ גַּם אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק נִקְרְאוּ "יִשְׂרָאֵל", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת), וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּטָּתָם שְׁלֵימָה.
records.originEnglish: “I will make your name great” corresponds to Jacob our father, who brought about the completeness of his offspring. This is “I will make your name great”: then the holiness of Abraham our father, the attribute of greatness, extended so as to endure forever—“A truthful lip will be established forever.” By then the refuse had departed, and it became clear that Abraham our father’s offspring too were complete, since Esau and Ishmael were not counted as his seed, as stated concerning Isaac, “Not all of Isaac.” After Jacob our father’s birth, Abraham and Isaac too were called “Israel,” as stated at the beginning of Toldot in Midrash Rabbah. That is, their offspring were complete.
records.targetHebrew: וְלֹא יָכְלָה לוֹ כִּי עָמַד נֶגְדּוֹ דְּמוּת דִּיּוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו (סוֹטָה ל״ו עַמּוּד ב׳) הַיְינוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁמּוֹרָשָׁה בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵהָאָבוֹת וְהָעִיקָּר יַעֲקֹב מוּבְחָר שֶׁבָּאָבוֹת, שֶׁכּוּלָּם נִקְרְאוּ עַל שְׁמוֹ כִּמְשַׁאזַ״ל (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס״ג:ב׳) כִּי כָל הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבָּהֶם הָיָה רַק מַה שֶּׁעָתִיד לָצֵאת מֵהֶם יַעֲקֹב שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה וְאֵין פְּסֹולֶת כְּלָל בְּזַרְעוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״יַעֲקֹב אֲשֶׁר פָּדָה אֶת אַבְרָהָם״ (יְשַׁעְיָה כ״ט:כ״ב) כִּי הוּא ״הַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכֹן [בְּתוֹךְ הַקְּרָשִׁים] מַבְרִחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה״ (שְׁמוֹת כ״ו:כ״ח) לִהְיוֹת דָּבוּק לְגַמְרֵי בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים עַד שֶׁאֵין מָקוֹם לְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת דְּסִטְרָא דְּרָע
records.targetEnglish: She could not overcome him, for the likeness of his father’s image stood before him. This is the root of holiness inherited in every soul of Israel from the fathers, principally Jacob, the choicest of the fathers, after whom all of them were named, as our Sages said. For all the holiness in them was on account of Jacob who would emerge from them, whose offspring were complete, with no refuse at all in his seed, as it says, “Jacob, who redeemed Abraham.” He is “the middle bar within the boards, passing through from end to end,” wholly attached to the living God, so that there is no room for the side of evil to spread.
records.explanation: Machshavot places the same ancestral claim inside Joseph’s trial. His father’s image is the inherited root that holds even under the temptation of Egypt. Thus the completeness attributed to Jacob explains the continuing efficacy of the earlier fathers’ holiness; it is not merely a change in family terminology. The full paragraph treats the brothers’ wrongdoing through its subsequent repair, so the quotation is not a declaration that every deed of every descendant is already good.

records.originHebrew: "וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ" – נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, שֶׁהוּא פָּעַל שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ", שֶׁאָז נִתְפַּשֵּׁט קְדֻשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מִדַּת גְּדוּלָּה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד, "שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד", שֶׁאָז כְּבָר יָצָא הַפְּסֹלֶת, וְאָז נִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁגַּם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, שֶׁעֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל לֹא נֶחְשַׁב זַרְעוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיִצְחָק "וְלֹא כָּל יִצְחָק", וְאַחַר לֵידַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ גַּם אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק נִקְרְאוּ "יִשְׂרָאֵל", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת), וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּטָּתָם שְׁלֵימָה.
records.originEnglish: “I will make your name great” corresponds to Jacob our father, who brought about the completeness of his offspring. This is “I will make your name great”: then the holiness of Abraham our father, the attribute of greatness, extended so as to endure forever—“A truthful lip will be established forever.” By then the refuse had departed, and it became clear that Abraham our father’s offspring too were complete, since Esau and Ishmael were not counted as his seed, as stated concerning Isaac, “Not all of Isaac.” After Jacob our father’s birth, Abraham and Isaac too were called “Israel,” as stated at the beginning of Toldot in Midrash Rabbah. That is, their offspring were complete.
records.targetHebrew: וכן איתא בש"ס (שבת קמ"ו.) עד שלשה דורות לא פסקה זוהמא מאבותינו. כי מאברהם ג"כ עוד נולד עוברי רצונו שיצא ממנו ישמעאל, וגם אמר לו ישמעאל יחיה לפניך, וכן מיצחק נולד עשו. ורק החילוק הוא שעליהם העיד השי"ת בתורתו, אשר אהבת את יצחק, שבלבבו אוהב את יצחק וכל התכלית שלו הוא רק יצחק. וכן, כי ביצחק יקרא לך זרע, ביצחק ולא כל יצחק, מאי משמע, שעליהם העיד השי"ת שכל עיקר הקמ"ל של שניהם הוא רק יעקב אבינו, שממנו לא יצא שום פסולת רק כולם עושי רצונו של מקום. ולזה אין קורין אבות אלא לשלשה, שעליהם החתים השי"ת שכל עיקר כוונתם הוא רק עושי רצונו.
records.targetEnglish: The Talmud likewise states: “The contamination did not cease from our fathers until three generations.” From Abraham too, transgressors of His will were still born, for Ishmael came from him, and he even said, “If only Ishmael might live before You.” Esau likewise was born from Isaac. The difference is that God testified concerning them in His Torah: “Whom you love, Isaac”—in his heart he loves Isaac, and his whole aim is Isaac alone. Likewise, “Through Isaac shall seed be called yours”—“through Isaac,” but not all of Isaac. What does this teach? God testified concerning them that the essential point of both is Jacob our father, from whom no refuse emerged, but all do the will of the Omnipresent. Therefore only the three are called fathers: concerning them God affixed His seal that their essential intention was directed only toward those who do His will.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef directly explains why Ishmael’s and Esau’s births do not prevent Abraham and Isaac from being counted among the fathers. Divine testimony identifies the line in which their deepest aim comes to expression. This clarifies Rav Tzadok’s retrospective statement that Jacob’s completeness also establishes the completeness of Abraham and Isaac; the target’s later distinction between present clarification and Adam’s future repair remains in its pinned context.

records.themeTitle: The priests’ distinct office draws its holiness from the whole people
records.themeSummary: Although only Levi’s descendants serve as priests, Rav Tzadok locates their power to bless in the holiness inherited from Abraham. Their distinct function does not make its source separate from Israel.
records.originHebrew: "וַאֲבָרְכָה מְבָרְכֶיךָ" – חָמֵשׁ, נֶגֶד קְדֻשַּׁת אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן, שֶׁלּוֹ נִיתַּן הַכֹּחַ לְבָרֵךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַאֲנִי אֲבָרְכֵם", שֶׁמַּשְׁפִּיעַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַבְּרָכוֹת לַכֹּהֲנִים שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְבָרֵךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל. וְזֶה הַכֹּחַ מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אַתָּה כֹהֵן לְעוֹלָם עַל דִּבְרָתִי מַלְכִּי צֶדֶק", שֶׁנִּדְרָשׁ (נְדָרִים לב עַמּוּד ב): שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהוֹצִיא כְּהֻנָּה מִשֵּׁם וְכוּלֵי וְעַל דִּבּוּרוֹ נְתָנָהּ לְאַבְרָהָם, עַיֵּין שָׁם. וְאַף שֶׁרַק מִזֶּרַע לֵוִי יָצְאוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים, וּשְׁאָר הַשְּׁבָטִים אֵינָם כֹּהֲנִים, רַק כֹּחַ הַכְּהֻנָּה שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו לְבָרֵךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל זֶהוּ רַק מִצַּד שֶׁהוּא מִזֶּרַע אַבְרָהָם וְלֹא בָּא מִכֹּחַ שֵׁם.
records.originEnglish: “I will bless those who bless you”—the fifth [blessing]—corresponds to the holiness of Aaron the priest, to whom the power to bless Israel was given, as it says, “And I will bless them”: the blessed God pours blessings upon the priests so that they can bless Israel. This power comes from Abraham our father. This is “You are a priest forever, on account of the words of Malki-Tzedek,” expounded in Nedarim: the Holy One wished to bring the priesthood forth from Shem … and on account of his words it was given to Abraham. See there. Although the priests came only from Levi’s descendants, while the other tribes are not priests, the priestly power given to Aaron and his sons to bless Israel comes solely from his being Abraham’s descendant; it does not come through Shem’s power.

records.targetEnglish: The Sanhedrin are called “the eyes of the congregation,” and the high priest is the head of the community. Likewise, all the holiness of priests and Levites is what emanates and is set apart from the holiness of the children of Israel. Although they were raised above them, this comes through Israel’s holiness, revealed more greatly in the tribe of Levi. This is the meaning of “Take the Levites from among the children of Israel.” Therefore, in the verse “I have given the Levites” in Behaalotekha, “the children of Israel” is said five times. Our Sages said, as cited in Rashi, that the fivefold mention in one verse makes known Israel’s belovedness. Why make it known specifically in that verse? So that we should not think the selection of the Levites from Israel implies a lack in Israel—that only the Levites were chosen for God’s service and all Israel were rejected as unfit for it. Precisely there it makes known their belovedness: the Levites were selected only through the great belovedness of Israel. Because of that belovedness, it was fitting for a tribe from among them to be chosen to serve Him. Without the intense belovedness of all Israel, no Levites would have been chosen at all. Their entire distinction is from within Israel and on account of Israel’s distinction and belovedness.
records.explanation: Divrei Soferim resolves the possible tension in Peri Tzadik’s final sentence. A selected tribe can perform a unique office while the holiness enabling it belongs to the whole community. This explains why identifying Aaron’s power with Abraham is compatible with reserving the priesthood to Levi; it does not erase the distinction of the priestly office.

records.targetHebrew: וְאַחַר זֶה הֵאִיר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֶת עֵינָיו לְהַרְאוֹת לוֹ כִּי חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לֹא נַעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שׁוּם דָּבָר לְבַטָּלָה, כִּי אַף אָמְנָם שֶׁמִּלּוֹט יָצְאוּ עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר עֲלֵיהֶם (אֵיכָה א, י): "לֹא יָבֹאוּ וְכוּלֵי", רַק זֹאת הוּא הַזְּכָרִים, אֲבָל נְקֵבוֹתֵיהֶם מוּתָּרוֹת מִיָּד, וְאַדְּרַבָּה, מִזֶּה נִצְמַח מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה אֲשֶׁר הֵם עִיקַּר קִיּוּם מְלוּכַת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וִירוּשָׁלַיִם; וְלָזֹאת אָמַר: "בָּרוּךְ אַבְרָם לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן". וְהִקְדִּים בִּרְכַּת אַבְרָהָם, כִּי גַּם אַבְרָהָם עָשָׂה פְּעוּלָּה לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגָתוֹ, רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵעִיר לִבּוֹ לָזֶה וְהוּא מָסַר אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ; וּלְפִי שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ נוֹדַע לוֹ זֹאת לְפִיכָךְ הִקְדִּים בִּרְכָתוֹ; וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִיטְּלָה מִמֶּנּוּ הַכְּהֻנָּה וְנִתְּנָה לְאַבְרָהָם (נְדָרִים לב עַמּוּד ב), כִּי הוֹדָה שֶׁאַבְרָהָם גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים קי, ד): "אַתָּה כֹהֵן לְעוֹלָם עַל דִּבְרָתִי מַלְכִּי צֶדֶק", הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֲנִי הֵאַרְתִּי עֵינָיו שֶׁל מַלְכִּי צֶדֶק שֶׁיִּרְאֶה שֶׁאַבְרָהָם גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ וְהוֹדָה מֵעַצְמוֹ.
records.targetEnglish: Afterward the blessed God enlightened his [Shem’s] eyes, showing him that, God forbid, nothing Abraham our father did was in vain. Although Ammon and Moab would emerge from Lot, concerning whom it is said, “They shall not enter [the congregation] …,” this applies only to the males; their females are permitted immediately. On the contrary, from this grew the kingdom of David and Solomon, who are the essential support of the kingdom of the land of Israel and Jerusalem. He therefore said, “Blessed is Abram of God Most High.” He put Abraham’s blessing first, for Abraham too had acted beyond his apprehension: God had awakened his heart to this, and he had risked his life. Because it became known to him through Abraham, he put Abraham’s blessing first. Through this the priesthood was taken from him and given to Abraham, for he acknowledged that Abraham was greater than he. Thus it says, “You are a priest forever, on account of the words of Malki-Tzedek”: I enlightened Malki-Tzedek’s eyes to see that Abraham was greater than he, and he acknowledged it of his own accord.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach supplies the narrative reasoning behind the transfer cited briefly by Rav Tzadok. Shem had questioned the rescue of Lot because he foresaw hostile descendants; he comes to recognize the future good that his initial judgment had missed. The priesthood passes with his acknowledgment of Abraham’s greater responsiveness to God. The qualification concerning female converts is retained because it is essential to the route from Lot to David.

records.themeTitle: One person’s restraint can strengthen the whole body of Israel
records.themeSummary: Joseph’s resistance in Egypt is credited with protecting all the males of Israel. The comparison explains why that effect is not confined to his own descendants.
records.originHebrew: "וּמְקַלֶּלְךָ אָאֹר" – שִׁית, וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יוֹסֵף, שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם, וְכָל מַאן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִקְרֵי צַדִּיק (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, כג עַמּוּד א), וְזֶהוּ כְּנֶגֶד בִּלְעָם שֶׁפָּרַץ גִּדְרוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם בַּעֲרָיוֹת, וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ, "זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה" בִּקְדוּשָׁה, יוֹסֵף, דְּאִיתָא (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד): יוֹסֵף יָרַד לְמִצְרַיִם וְגָדַר עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעֶרְוָה, וְנִגְדְּרוּ כָּל הַזְּכָרִים בִּזְכוּתוֹ; וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר "וּמְקַלֶּלְךָ אָאֹר" עַל בִּלְעָם.
records.originEnglish: “And your curser I will curse”—the sixth [blessing]—corresponds to Joseph, whose attribute is “the righteous one, the foundation of the world”; and “everyone who is circumcised is called righteous.” This stands against Balaam, who breached the world’s boundary in sexual immorality. Corresponding to him on the side of holiness is Joseph, for Shir HaShirim Rabbah states: Joseph went down to Egypt and fenced himself against sexual transgression, and all the males were fenced through his merit. Concerning Balaam, therefore, it says, “And your curser I will curse.”
records.targetHebrew: כַּאֲשֶׁר הָאָדָם גּוֹדֵר עַצְמוֹ בְּאֵיזֶה דָבָר לְהִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגֶד יִצְרוֹ בְּכָל כֹּחוֹ, הוּא גּוֹדֵר בְּכֹחוֹ זֶה כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מֵאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית שֶׁבְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת בְּאוֹתוֹ דָבָר, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל״ב] וּבְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה [עַל פָּסוּק "גַּן נָעוּל"]: שָׂרָה יָרְדָה לְמִצְרַיִם וְגָדְרָה עַצְמָהּ מִן הָעֶרְוָה וְכָל הַנָּשִׁים נִגְדְּרוּ בִּזְכוּתָהּ, וְיוֹסֵף יָרַד לְמִצְרַיִם וְגָדַר עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעֶרְוָה וְנִגְדְּרוּ כָּל הַזְּכָרִים בִּזְכוּתוֹ; וְאִם בְּשָׂרָה יֵשׁ לוֹמַר לְפִי שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִזַּרְעָהּ וְצֶאֱצָאֶיהָ, בְּיוֹסֵף לֹא שַׁיָּךְ זֶה, וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ לְפִי שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹמָה אַחַת, וּבִשְׁלֵמוּת הָאֶחָד נִשְׁלָם כָּל הַקּוֹמָה. וְאָמַר יָרְדוּ לְמִצְרַיִם הַיְינוּ דְּנִכְנְסוּ לְנִסָּיוֹן דְּשָׁם "עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ", מְקוֹם תֹּקֶף הַקְּלִפָּה דַּעֲרָיוֹת, וְהַגְדָּרַת עֶרְוָה דְּשָׁם הַיְינוּ חֲסָרַת כָּל תֹּקֶף כֹּחַ אוֹתָהּ קְלִפָּה וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִגְדְּרוּ הַכֹּל;
records.targetEnglish: When a person fences himself in some matter, striving with all his strength against his inclination, by this power he fences all the souls of the Israelite nation in all generations in that matter. Thus the Sages said: Sarah went down to Egypt and fenced herself against sexual transgression, and all the women were fenced through her merit; Joseph went down to Egypt and fenced himself against sexual transgression, and all the males were fenced through his merit. In Sarah’s case one could say that this is because all Israel are her seed and descendants. That does not apply to Joseph. It must therefore be because all Israel are one complete body: when one part is perfected, the entire body is perfected. “They went down to Egypt” means that they entered a trial there, in “the nakedness of the land,” the place where the shell of sexual transgression is most powerful. Fencing against sexual transgression there means depriving that shell of all its strength; through this everyone was fenced.
records.explanation: Divrei Soferim asks the exact question left implicit in the cited Midrash: Joseph is not the ancestor of every Israelite male. His effect therefore rests on the unity of the people, not merely on biological inheritance. The full target paragraph distinguishes this inner strengthening from the fact that actual transgressions still occur, so the connection does not claim that later people have lost the ability to sin.

records.themeTitle: The receiving community seeks completion from its holy source
records.themeSummary: The seventh blessing describes influence flowing through Yesod into the congregation of Israel. The change from dalet to hei depicts the receiving side becoming filled; conversion brings a willing entrant into that community under the stated covenantal conditions.
records.originHebrew: "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה" – הָא שֶׁבַע, נֶגֶד מִדַּת מַלְכוּת שֶׁדָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מֶרְכָּבָה לָהּ, וְהוּא שֶׁעַל יְדֵי מִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם בָּא הַהַשְׁפָּעָה לְמִדַּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, קעח עַמּוּד ב): "הֵ"א, דָּלֶ"ת הֲוַת בְּקַדְמִיתָא, וּמִדְּאִתְעַבְּרַת בֵּיהּ בְּגַוַּוהּ וְכוּלֵי", וְהַיְינוּ יוֹ"ד שֶׁל שֵׁם שַׁדַּ"י וְאָז נַעֲשָׂה הֵ"א, וְהַיְינוּ דְּכָל מַאן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִקְרֵי צַדִּיק. וּכְתִיב: "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה", שֶׁאַף מֵעוֹבְדֵי כוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת מִי שֶׁיִּרְצֶה לְהִכָּנֵס בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְיָמוּל אֶת עַצְמוֹ וִיקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל הַמִּצְווֹת, בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכֻנֶּה, וְיִהְיֶה בִּכְלַל "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים וְגוֹמֵר".
records.originEnglish: “All the families of the earth shall be blessed through you”—these are seven. It corresponds to the attribute of kingship, for which King David is a chariot. Through the attribute of the righteous one, the foundation of the world, influence comes to the attribute of the congregation of Israel. As the Zohar states: “Hei was originally dalet; and when it became pregnant with [the letter] within it ….” This is the yud of the name Shaddai, and then it becomes hei: “everyone who is circumcised is called righteous.” It is written, “All the families of the earth shall be blessed through you”: even among idolaters, one who wishes to enter Israel, circumcises himself, and accepts the yoke of the commandments will be designated by the name Israel and included in “Your people are all righteous ….”
records.targetHebrew: וּבְהַקְדָּמַת הַזֹּהַר דְּקוֹ״ף רֵי״שׁ אַתְוָון דְּשִׁקְרָא, פֵּירוּשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, קעח עַמּוּד ב) דְּהֵ״א דָּלֶ״ת הֲוַות, רַק בָּתַר דִּקְבִילַת עוּבָּרָא נַעֲשָׂה הֵ״א. וּבִפְרִי עֵץ חַיִּים רֵישׁ שַׁעַר הַשַּׁבָּת דְּכֵן גַּם כֵּן אוֹת קוֹ״ף רֵי״שׁ הֲוַות וְכוּלֵי, פֵּירוּשׁ לְשׁוֹן דַּלּוּת וְרֵישׁ אֶחָד, דְּמוֹרֶה עַל עֲנִיּוּת וְחִסָּרוֹן, דְּלֵית לָהּ מִגַּרְמָהּ וּמְבַקֶּשֶׁת הַשְׁלָמָה. רַק שֶׁזֶּה צוּרָתוֹ בְּקַוִּים יְשָׁרִים וְזֶה בַּעֲקַמְמוּמִיּוּת. כִּי זֶה מִתְאַוֶּוה רַק לְהַשְׁפָּעַת קַו הַיּוֹשֶׁר דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְכֵן הָעוּבָּר דִּקְבִילַת כֵּן בְּקַו הַיּוֹשֶׁר, וְזוֹ בַּעֲקַמְמוּמִיּוּת.
records.targetEnglish: In the introduction to the Zohar, kuf and resh are the letters of falsehood. The explanation follows what the Zohar says: hei was dalet, and only after it received an embryo did it become hei. At the beginning of the Gate of Shabbat in Pri Etz Chaim it says that kuf likewise was resh. That is, dalut and resh mean the same thing: they indicate poverty and lack, having nothing of their own and seeking completion. But the form of one is made with straight lines, while the other is curved. For the one longs only for the influence of God’s straight line, and the embryo it receives is likewise along the straight line; the other is curved.
records.explanation: Tzidkat explains the inner meaning of the letter image cited in Peri Tzadik: lack can become a receptive longing for completion from God. This clarifies the movement of influence into the congregation of Israel, beyond merely counting the strokes of dalet and hei. The source’s admission of a convert and its requirements remain Peri Tzadik’s own explicit teaching; this excerpt from Tzidkat does not itself state those requirements.

records.themeTitle: The completed blessing joins the first root to its final expression
records.themeSummary: Rav Tzadok reconciles the fourfold and sevenfold accounts by distinguishing the gift that reaches the whole community from its particular expression in David’s kingship. Related accounts of a blessing can describe complementary positions within one movement.
records.originHebrew: וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חָשַׁב אַרְבַּע בְּרָכוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת נֶגֶד אַרְבַּע רַגְלֵי הַמֶּרְכָּבָה, וְחָשַׁב שָׁלֹשׁ כְּנֶגֶד יְמִינָא וּשְׂמָאלָא וְעַמּוּדָא דְּאֶמְצָעִיתָא, וְהֵם מִדּוֹת חֶסֶד, גְּבוּרָה, תִּפְאֶרֶת שֶׁהָאָבוֹת מֶרְכָּבָה לָהֶן, וְ"הֶיֵה בְרָכָה" מִסִּטְרָא דְּאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהַיְינוּ מִדַּת מַלְכוּת, כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל. וְאַף דִּלְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְנוּ "וֶהְיֵה בְרָכָה" נֶגֶד מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, אַךְ הַמְּכֻוָּון "וֶהְיֵה בְרָכָה" נֶגֶד מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ שֶׁהוֹפִיעַ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה, וְעַל יְדֵי כֵן "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה", שֶׁאַף הַשָּׁפֵל שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּמְשַׁל לַאֲדָמָה יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה, כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "מוֹרָשָׁה קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב", וְכָאָמוּר; אֲבָל הַבְּרָכָה הַמְּיוּחֶדֶת שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד מִדַּת מַלְכוּת שֶׁדָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מֶרְכָּבָה לָהּ, הוּא "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ וְגוֹמֵר", כְּמוֹ שֶׁחָשַׁב בְּסִטְרֵי תּוֹרָה בְּרָכָה שְׁבִיעִית, וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד.
records.originEnglish: The holy Zohar counts the first four blessings against the four legs of the chariot: three against right, left, and the central column—the attributes of kindness, strength, and beauty, for which the fathers are a chariot—and “Be a blessing” from the side of the land of Israel, meaning kingship, the congregation of Israel. Although, according to what we wrote, “Be a blessing” corresponds to Moses our teacher, its meaning is that Moses brought the blessing into Israel whereby every Israelite has a share in Torah. Through this, “All the families of the earth shall be blessed through you”: even the lowliest Israelite, likened to earth, has a share in Torah, as it says, “An inheritance of the congregation of Jacob,” as explained. But the specific blessing corresponding to kingship, for which King David is a chariot, is “All … shall be blessed through you,” as Sitrei Torah counts the seventh blessing. It is all one.
records.targetHebrew: "וֶהְיֵה בְּרָכָה" – בְּךָ חוֹתְמִין פְּסָחִים קיז:, וְכֵן בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה. כִּי אַבְרָהָם – רֹאשׁ הַבְּרִיאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרָכוֹת טז:: "אֵין קוֹרִין אָבוֹת אֶלָּא לִשְׁלֹשָׁה", שֶׁהֵם אֲבוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְהַהַתְחָלָה מֵהַכָּרַת הָאֱלֹהוּת, וְאַבְרָהָם – אָב לְכוּלָּם, כִּי "אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם וְגוֹמֵר" בְּרֵאשִׁית יז, ה, נִכְלַל תֹּאַר "אָב" בִּשְׁמוֹ כִּי "אָב" רָצָה לוֹמַר: הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת לָעֲנָפִים, וְהוּא מִמִּדַּת הַחֶסֶד שֶׁהוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת. וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר חֵלֶק ג, רנו עַמּוּד ב: "אַבָּא יָסַד בְּרַתָּא", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר, כִּי אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק, יַעֲקֹב, וְדָוִד אָב, וְאֵם, בֵּן, וּבַת; וְ"סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה", כִּי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא מָשִׁיחַ, הוּא סוֹף הַבְּרִיאָה, וּלְכָךְ בּוֹ חֲתִימַת הַבְּרָכָה מִתְיַיחֵס לְהַתְחָלַת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה.
records.targetEnglish: “Be a blessing”—the blessing concludes with you; and likewise with King David, as our Sages taught. For Abraham is the beginning of creation: “Only three are called fathers.” They are the fathers of the world and the beginning of the recognition of divinity, and Abraham is father to them all, for “I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.” The designation “father” is included in his name, for “father” means an extension into branches, from the attribute of kindness, which is extension. The Zohar states, “The father founded the daughter,” as I have written elsewhere: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and David are father, mother, son, and daughter. “The final act is first in thought”: King David, who is Messiah, is the end of creation. Therefore the blessing’s conclusion with him is related to the beginning of thought.
records.explanation: Kometz shows how Abraham and David can both be associated with the conclusion of blessing: the final realization expresses what was present at the first root. This gives a model for the complementary mappings in Peri Tzadik. It does not substitute Kometz’s family imagery for Peri Tzadik’s specific explanation of Moses’ gift of Torah to the whole community.

records.themeTitle: Kingship is the enduring imprint in the receiving community
records.themeSummary: The fourth blessing can name the land of Israel and kingship while the sevenfold account separately names Moses and David. Rav Tzadok explains this through Torah becoming the possession of every member of the community.

records.targetEnglish: This is what the holy Zohar states: “‘Be a blessing’—from the side of the land of Israel.” It is the attribute of the kingdom of Heaven, for this is the quality established in that attribute. Concerning all the attributes it is said: “When You withdraw from them, they remain like a body without a soul.” But concerning the kingdom of Heaven the Zohar states: “‘Set me as a seal upon your heart.’ The way of a seal is that, once it adheres to the place to which it adheres, it leaves all its image there. Although that seal goes here and there … it leaves all its image there, and there it remains.”
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov explains why the land/kingship interpretation describes an enduring receiver: the image remains as a seal’s impression. This illuminates the stable communal possession underlying Rav Tzadok’s reconciliation—Torah has been given to every Israelite. The target explains the quality of kingship; Peri Tzadik supplies the particular identification of the giver as Moses.

records.themeTitle: Circumcision reveals a holiness prior to conscious service
records.themeSummary: The infant’s covenant before conscious choice indicates an enduring root in divine thought. That root explains why the name Israel survives later wrongdoing.
records.originHebrew: דְּאָסָא מָצִינוּ (מְגִילָּה יג עַמּוּד א): "הַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ הֲדַסִּים", וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים". וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (צג עַמּוּד א): "וְהָא כַּמָּה חַיָּיבִין אִית בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כַּמָּה חַטָּאִין וְכַמָּה רְשִׁיעִין וְכוּלֵי, אֶלָּא וְכוּלֵי, דִּמְקָרְבִין בְּנַיְיהוּ לִתְמַנְיָא יוֹמִין לְקָרְבָּנָא, וְכַד אִתְגְּזַרוּ וְכוּלֵי אִקְרוּן צַדִּיקִים וְכוּלֵי", וְהַיְינוּ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד עַמּוּד א) עַל הַפָּסוּק "חָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל": "אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא – יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא; אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרֵי אִינָשֵׁי: אָסָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּינֵי חִילְפֵי, אָסָא שְׁמֵיהּ וְאָסָא קָרוּ לֵיהּ". וְהוּא, שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּימּוֹל הַתִּינוֹק לִשְׁמוֹנָה שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ וְנַעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי כֵן יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְזֶה מוֹרֶה שֶׁקָּשׁוּר בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, וְכָל מַה שֶּׁעוֹבֵר עָלָיו, בֶּאֱמֶת: "רְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב? שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה וְכוּלֵי", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת יז עַמּוּד א).
records.originEnglish: Concerning myrtle, we find: “The righteous are called myrtles.” All Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it says, “Your people are all righteous.” The holy Zohar in this portion asks: “But how many guilty people there are in Israel, how many sinners and how many wicked people!” It answers that they bring their children at eight days old as an offering, and when they are circumcised they are called righteous. This accords with what the Talmud says about “Israel has sinned”: “Even though he has sinned, he is still Israel.” Rabbi Abba said: This is what people say: “A myrtle standing among the thorn bushes is named a myrtle, and a myrtle they call it.” Since the infant is circumcised at eight days without his conscious choice and thereby becomes Israel, this indicates that he is bound at his root to the blessed God, in the beginning of divine thought. Whatever he undergoes, the truth is: “Our will is to do Your will; what prevents us? The leaven in the dough,” and so forth, as written in Berakhot.
records.targetHebrew: וְזֶה הוּא שֶׁהַנּוּסַח (מִבִּרְכַּת בְּרִית מִילָה) הוּא: "אֲשֶׁר קִדַּשׁ יְדִיד מִבֶּטֶן", חוּץ מֵהַבְּרָכָה שֶׁהָאָב מְבָרֵךְ; וְלָמָּה נִשְׁתַּנָּה זוֹ הַבְּרָכָה מִכָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת שֶׁהַנּוּסַח הוּא "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ"? אָכֵן מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאוֹת יוּ"ד אֵין לָהּ שׁוּם צוּרָה מִצַּד עַצְמָהּ, כִּי הִיא כְּלוּלָה בְּעַצְמוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְמַעְלָה מִתְּפִיסַת שֵׂכֶל הָאָדָם, וּמִצְוַת מִילָה הִיא גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשָּׁה מִבֶּטֶן לְמַעְלָה מִתְּפִיסַת שֵׂכֶל הָאָדָם; לָכֵן מְבָרְכִין "אֲשֶׁר קִדַּשׁ יְדִיד מִבֶּטֶן" – שֶׁבְּמִצְוַת מִילָה מִתְגַּלֶּה שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵם מִבֶּטֶן וּמִלֵּידָה לְמַעְלָה מִכֹּחַ עֲבוֹדָה, בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא יַשִּׂיג כֹּחַ עֲבוֹדַת אָדָם; מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּכָל שְׁאָר הַמִּצְווֹת, שֶׁהַקְּדוּשָּׁה הִיא מִצַּד הָאָדָם שֶׁמְּקַדֵּשׁ אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִצִּדּוֹ בְּכֹחַ עֲבוֹדָתוֹ, לָכֵן מְבָרְכִינַן "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ".
records.targetEnglish: This is why the formula [in the blessing of circumcision] is “Who sanctified the beloved one from the womb,” apart from the blessing that the father recites. Why does this blessing differ from all the blessings whose formula is “Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us”? Because the letter yud has no form of its own: it is included in His essence, beyond the apprehension of human understanding. The commandment of circumcision likewise is holiness from the womb, beyond the apprehension of human understanding. Therefore we bless, “Who sanctified the beloved one from the womb”: through circumcision it becomes manifest that Israel are holy from the womb and from birth, beyond the power of service, in a place the power of human service cannot reach. In all the other commandments, however, the holiness is from the person who sanctifies himself through his own power of service. Therefore we bless, “Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us.”
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov draws the same distinction from the wording of the circumcision blessing. The covenant reveals a holiness already rooted before a person’s conscious work, whereas the ordinary blessing names sanctification through the person’s commanded action. This gives a concrete ritual expression to Rav Tzadok’s inference from circumcision at eight days; it does not make later obedience or repentance unnecessary.

records.themeTitle: The strongest accusation does not uproot Israel’s name
records.themeSummary: The severe descriptions of Achan establish the reach of the claim “even though he sinned, he is Israel.” Rav Tzadok preserves the reality of wrongdoing while denying that it can erase the root.
records.originHebrew: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא שָׁם עַל עָכָן שֶׁעָבַר עַל חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי, מוֹשֵׁךְ בְּעָרְלָתוֹ הָיָה וְכַדּוֹמֶה, וְלָמָּה דָּרְשׁוּ בּוֹ כָּל כָּךְ לִגְנַאי? אַךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁבְּעָכָן נִכְתַּב "חָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל", לְהַשְׁמִיעֵנוּ זֶה שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא, מִשּׁוּם הָכִי תָּלוּ עָלָיו כָּל מַה שֶּׁיּוּכְלוּ לִתְלוֹת מֵהָרַע, לְלַמֵּד שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁעוֹבֵר עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, מִכָּל מָקוֹם "לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח", שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ.
records.originEnglish: This is what the Talmud there says concerning Achan: that he transgressed the Five Books of Torah … that he drew out his foreskin, and the like. Why did they interpret him so extensively to his discredit? Since concerning Achan it is written, “Israel has sinned,” to teach that even though he sinned, he is Israel, they attributed to him every evil they could attribute. This teaches that, whatever an Israelite undergoes, nevertheless “none shall be cast away from Him”: the name Israel is not uprooted from him.
records.targetHebrew: רַק שֶׁזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אֵין יְכוֹלִים עוֹד לְהַחֲלִיף שְׁמָם וְלַעֲקֹר עַצְמָם מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת, וַאֲפִילּוּ יַגְדִּילוּ עֲוֹנוֹת עַד לַשָּׁמַיִם, עֲדַיִן יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא לְכָל דָּבָר, וְלֹא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ, שֶׁהוּא הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁבְּכָל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב דְּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, שֶׁאֵין בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ שֶׁבְּכָל זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו שׁוּם פְּסֹלֶת, וְעַל כֵּן זֶה הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ דְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמִּיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נִשְׁאָר לְעוֹלָם; אֲבָל עֵשָׂו, אַף דְּנוֹלַד בִּקְדוּשָּׁה, עֲדַיִן הָיָה הַבְּחִירָה בְּיָדוֹ לַעֲקֹר עַצְמוֹ מִקְּדוּשָּׁה זוֹ שֶׁיָּרַשׁ מֵאֲבוֹתָיו.
records.targetEnglish: But the seed of Jacob our father can no longer change their name and uproot themselves from the root of Jewishness. Even if their transgressions grow to the heavens, they are still Israel in every respect. The name Israel is not uprooted from them: it is the holy root in all Jacob’s seed, whose offspring are complete, with no refuse in the root from which all his subsequent seed come. Therefore this root of the name Israel, from Jacob our father, remains forever. Esau, however, although born in holiness, still had the choice to uproot himself from the holiness he had inherited from his fathers.
records.explanation: Divrei Soferim makes explicit the distinction on which the Achan argument rests: the name Israel belongs to an enduring root, while wrongdoing is judged in its actual manifestation. Its contrast with Esau explains why outward similarity does not establish identical spiritual roots. The target’s full paragraph expressly retains the sphere of judgment; the connection does not turn Achan’s acts into permitted acts.
